notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.

Each year on April 28th we pause at 11:00 a.m. to remember workers who have died, were injured or became ill from their jobs. At the City of Waterloo, we honour the memory of Don Klassen, a Building Inspector, who passed from a work-related injury in 1990; Grant Bettke, a Fire Fighter who passed from work-related cancer in 2015; and Donald Schmitt, a Fire Fighter who passed from work-related cancer in 2025. We also take this time to reflect on all former and current City employees who have been, and continue to be, impacted by workplace injuries and illnesses. This day serves as an opportunity for all workers to collectively renew our commitment to improving health and safety, so we can prevent workplace injuries, illnesses, and fatalities.

Please join us in observing the Day of Mourning to remember those impacted by workplace tragedy and to re-commit to improving physical and psychological health and safety at the City. All flags at City facilities will be half-masted tomorrow from sunrise to sunset.

items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.
Mayor McCabe provided Council with a further moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: University of Waterloo
notes: Nick Manning, Associate Vice-President, Communications and Institutional Relations, University of Waterloo gave a presentation emphasizing the University’s strong partnership with the City, its role in creating jobs and innovation, and its success in attracting and retaining talent in the City of Waterloo. Nick Manning then responded to questions from Council.

items.title: Items Removed From the Consent Motion
2026 Business Improvement Area Levy
notes: Jeyas Balaskanthan, Executive Director, Uptown Waterloo Business Improvement Area gave a presentation highlighting the strong growth in Uptown, including growth in events, business participation and local economic impact. He also emphasized Uptown’s continued expansion through new businesses, festivals and partnerships, focusing on safety, cleanliness and community vibrancy. He then responded to questions from Council.

items.title: Consideration of Notice of Motion Given at Previous Meeting
Councillor Roe – Heritage Helping Housing Motion
notes: Motion tabled April 20, 2026 for Council consideration April 27, 2026.

Kae Elgie, Government and Community Relations Committee Member, Architectural Conservancy Ontario gave a presentation on proposed provincial grant programs to help convert heritage properties into affordable housing units, which would fund a portion of renovation costs for adaptive reuse projects. Kae Elgie then responded to questions of Council.

motions.item_title: Councillor Roe – Heritage Helping Housing Motion
motions.text: WHEREAS Architectural Conservancy Ontario (ACO) is the province’s leading non-governmental organization dedicated to the conservation and reuse of Ontario’s built and cultural heritage; through education and advocacy ACO encourages the prevention and adaptive reuse of buildings and landscapes of architectural, historic and cultural significance; WHEREAS ACO has emphasized that strong heritage protections are compatible with and supportive of efforts to address Ontario’s housing crisis, particularly through the retention, rehabilitation and repurposing of older building for new residential uses; WHEREAS heritage buildings can help solve Ontario’s housing crisis by offering solutions that are affordable, equitable, sustainable and uniquely Canadian; including the repair and reuse of existing buildings which provides faster, cheaper and a more sustainable path to creating affordable housing and by enabling the delivery of homes faster than new construction while also supporting a stronger jobs market; WHEREAS older and heritage buildings represent an important and often underutilized opportunity to create additional housing units, provided that appropriate financial incentives exist to support renovation and code- compliance upgrades; WHEREAS ACO has proposed that the Province of Ontario implement a new housing-focused “Heritage Helping Housing Building Grant” of $10 million per year to encourage property owners and developers to rehabilitate and make adaptive reuse of heritage buildings that creates new housing units; WHEREAS such a provincial grant program would support municipal housing objectives, help revitalize main streets, encourage private investment, reduce demolition waste, and strengthen the economic and cultural vitality of Ontario communities; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that this Council request the Mayor send a letter to the Hon. Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, with copies to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, The Hon. Rob Flack, the Minister of Finance, the Hon. Peter Bethlenfalvy, the Minister of Citizenship and Multiculturalism, the Hon. Graham McGregor and John Ecker, Chair, Ontario Heritage Trust, requesting that the Province of Ontario establish the Heritage Helping Housing Building Grant as proposed by the ACO, and that a copy of this resolution be circulated to local and area MPPs and heads of council.
